overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate and insufficient minutes for its May 24 meeting; a member did not violate the law by copying the Board on a complaint filed with the AG.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the May 24 meeting were alleged to be inaccurate and insufficient: they misstated a member's objection, omitted a ten-minute email discussion, and omitted motions.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate and insufficient meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: A complaint alleged a topic (the emergency beaver permit) was discussed at the May 24 meeting without being on the posted notice; the request for further review recast the issue as one about minutes.
allegations.key_passage: In the request for further review, Mr. Kelleher clarified that his concerns relate to the sufficiency of the minutes for the Board’s May 24 meeting which were approved during the Board’s May 31 meeting.

allegations.summary: A member was alleged to have deliberated improperly by copying the full Board on an email filing an Open Meeting Law complaint with the Attorney General for further review.
allegations.key_passage: It is appropriate for a complainant to copy the public body that is the subject of the complaint when filing the complaint with the Attorney General’s Office.

allegations.summary: Allegations raised outside the formal complaints, including in the request for further review, were not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complainants raise additional allegations outside of their  formal Open Meeting Law complaints, we decline to review such allegations.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
Within 30 days of the determination, amend the minutes of the May 24 meeting to ensure compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Board, within 30 days of the date of this determination, to amend the minutes of its May 24 meeting to ensure compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
